scenarios.title: Protect the puck beside the boards
scenarios.objective: Use the board side and a support player to protect a carry under pressure.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the +x end and gold attacks the -x end. YOU control the puck beside the boards in the attacking end. Gold1 approaches from the middle. Navy2 waits inside near the faceoff circle. The coach asks you to protect, then look inside.
cues: YOU control the puck by the boards.
Navy2 waits near the faceoff circle.

questions.prompt: Who controls the puck?
questions.explanation: YOU are the puck owner by the boards. Gold1 is pressure and Navy2 is support.

questions.prompt: What should shape your next touch?
questions.explanation: Gold1's approach and Navy2's location show the pressure and support picture. No escape is guaranteed.

questions.prompt: Place YOU a little closer to the boards with Gold1 in view.
questions.explanation: This example gives YOU board-side protection while keeping the defender visible. A safe position depends on the live lane.

questions.prompt: Arrange this board-side read.

options.text: Protect the puck on the far side

questions.explanation: Read where pressure comes from, protect away from it, then scan for Navy2 or space. The choices connect the named players to the puck.

questions.prompt: Gold1 reaches the boards. What could YOU try?

options.text: Look inside for Navy2 or a new lane

questions.explanation: Gold1 changed the board-side lane. Navy2 or another clear lane may now be safer, depending on the new pressure.

questions.prompt: Why can the boards help protect the puck?
questions.explanation: The boards give pressure fewer directions to reach from, while YOU can keep your body between Gold1 and the puck. You still need to see Navy2 and the changing lane.

scenarios.title: Give the middle a passing target
scenarios.objective: Find space between pressure players and offer a visible middle option.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the +x end and gold attacks the -x end. YOU have the puck near the side. Navy2 is wide ahead. Gold1 is between YOU and Navy2. Gold2 is farther toward the net. The coach asks you to compare the middle and wide options.
cues: Gold1 is between YOU and Navy2.
Gold2 is farther toward the net.

questions.prompt: Who has the puck?

questions.prompt: Which players affect the first pass?

options.text: A player who is not shown

questions.explanation: Gold1 blocks the direct lane to Navy2, while Navy2 is a real visible target. Gold2 is an opponent farther ahead, but the first lane is the key cue.

questions.prompt: Place YOU in the middle with Navy2 still visible.
questions.explanation: This example changes the angle around Gold1 and keeps the wide teammate visible. Another open position can work if the lane remains clear.

questions.prompt: Arrange the middle-option read.

options.text: Carry or pass after checking space

questions.explanation: The teammate and defender define the choice. A small move can change the lane, but the puck action still needs a new check.

questions.prompt: Gold1 moves with YOU toward the middle. What could change?

options.text: Use Navy2 only if the new lane is clear, or carry
Pass through Gold1 because Navy2 is open

questions.explanation: Gold1 remains part of the lane after following. Navy2 may still be useful, but only if the lane is open; carrying is another conditional choice.

questions.prompt: Why can moving change a passing lane?
questions.explanation: A new angle can move Gold1 out of the direct line or can bring the defender into it. YOU must use the positions of Gold1 and Navy2 now, not the first picture.

scenarios.title: Support the breakout side
scenarios.objective: Choose a support lane that helps a carrier exit pressure near the defending end.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the +x end and gold attacks the -x end. Navy2 has the puck near the navy end boards. YOU are below the puck. Gold1 is between the carrier and the middle. Navy3 waits near the blue line. The coach asks you to become a safe outlet.
cues: Navy2 has the puck near the navy end boards.
Gold1 sits between Navy2 and the middle.
Navy3 waits near the blue line.

questions.prompt: Who has the puck near the boards?
questions.explanation: Navy2 controls the puck. YOU can become an outlet while Gold1 applies pressure.

questions.prompt: Which details help YOU support?

options.text: Gold1 between Navy2 and middle ice
A fixed route no matter what

questions.explanation: Gold1's position makes the middle lane harder, and Navy3 is a visible higher option. The route must adapt to pressure.

questions.prompt: Place YOU between Navy2 and the lower-side space, where the carrier can see you.
questions.explanation: This example gives Navy2 a lower-side outlet while keeping YOU away from Gold1's middle line. Another clear support lane can work.

questions.prompt: Arrange the breakout support read.

options.text: Offer a clear outlet and check Navy3

questions.explanation: Locate the carrier, read pressure, then offer a lane that helps. Navy3 gives another reference for the next choice.

questions.prompt: Gold1 turns toward your outlet. What might Navy2 use?
questions.explanation: Gold1 changed the outlet. Navy3 or another lane may be safer if the carrier can see it and pressure permits.

questions.prompt: Why can a lower outlet help the carrier?
questions.explanation: Gold1 is between Navy2 and the middle, so a lower-side option can give the carrier a different angle. The carrier still has to check whether YOU remain open.

scenarios.title: Read the loose puck after a block
scenarios.objective: Update ownership and support after a defender blocks a pass.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the +x end and gold attacks the -x end. Navy2 tried to pass to YOU, but Gold1 touched the puck and it is loose. YOU are nearest the puck. Navy3 is open on the far side. Gold2 is behind YOU.
cues: Navy3 is on the far side and Gold2 is behind YOU.

questions.prompt: Gold1 controls the puck before YOU arrive. What changes?

options.text: Navy players need a new defensive read
YOU still have the planned pass

questions.explanation: Gold1 becoming the owner changes the role picture. Navy players should read the carrier and protect their end before choosing a response.

questions.prompt: Why can the old pass plan disappear?
questions.explanation: Gold1 touched the pass and the puck became loose. Ownership, pressure, and Navy3's support must be checked again before repeating the old plan.

questions.prompt: Who has the puck?
questions.explanation: Gold1 controls the puck. Navy2 is pressuring and YOU can support the play away from the puck.

questions.prompt: Who should YOU keep in view?
questions.explanation: The puck carrier and far-side attacker both shape the defensive choice. Watching only Navy2 loses Gold2.

questions.prompt: Place YOU between Gold2 and the navy end, with Gold1 visible.
questions.explanation: This example brings YOU into a support line that can see the puck and far-side player. The moving play may call for a different lane.

questions.prompt: Arrange the away-side support read.
questions.explanation: Start with the puck carrier, then read the first defender, then see the away-side option. This prevents chasing the same player twice.

questions.prompt: Gold2 cuts toward the puck side. What changes for YOU?

options.text: Keep both gold players in view and adjust

questions.explanation: Gold2's movement changes the support picture. Adjust while keeping Gold1 and Gold2 visible so the nearer defender gets useful help.

questions.prompt: Why can the far-side player matter?
questions.explanation: Gold2 can become a pass option while Navy2 pressures Gold1. Seeing away from the puck helps YOU choose where support is needed.
